understand.clutterMap:
The Run console reads as **deeply messy** because of **FOUR full-width bordered horizontal toolbars stacked before the scoreboard** (lines 1264, 1439, 1443, 1449), each with **competing visual hierarchies** and **redundant labeling**:

1. **4 competing border styles**: slate-50 bg + border-slate-200 (Strip 1), white bg + border-slate-200 (Strip 2), slate-900 bg + border-slate-800 (Strip 3), slate-50 bg + border-slate-200 (Strip 4) — no visual grouping, looks like a disorganized deck of cards.

2. **Vertical space cost**: ~40-44px per strip × 4 = **160-176px wasted on chrome BEFORE the operator even sees the scoreboard** on a laptop running 1080p. The scoreboard itself is only ~240-300px tall in Full view due to the console-fit density downshift (useConsoleFit, line 1251). This means on a typical 1080p display, the operator LOSES 50-60% of the screen height to chrome labels + borders.

3. **No visual hierarchy**: Every pill, button, and label uses the same Tailwind color tokens (text-[11px], text-[13px]) with NO distinction between:
   - **Primary actions** (Go Live, score controls, clock) which belong front-and-center
   - **Secondary actions** (scene recall, cue firing) which are important but not constant
   - **Status/ambient** (screen health, game state label) which should be glanceable, not intrusive

4. **Redundant labeling**: Three separate label rows ("Switch view", "Game state", "Screens", "Show on board") each repeat the same small-caps uppercase pattern, creating visual noise. The operator's eye has to scan 4 separate label→control clusters instead of one unified command surface.

5. **Horizontal scrolling on mobile**: Strips 1, 3, 4 all carry `overflow-x-auto` pills that force right-scrolling on smaller tablets — the operator reaches for a second action (Spotlight, Back to Live) and the rail scrolls, burying what they just tapped.

6. **No spatial grouping**: The 4 strips are visually isolated (each has its own `flex items-center`, `border-b`, unique `bg-*`). There's no visual frame saying "these 4 things work together as the operator console"; they read as 4 unrelated toolbars in a Firefox extension.

**Why it reads as messy, not "just cluttered"**: In Daktronics, CTS, GameChanger, and ScoreVision, the operator console is ONE cohesive command surface (often a single row or a left sidebar) with:
- A big clock/score in the center
- Grouped contextual buttons in clear sections (status / actions / surfaces)
- Status lights at the edges (not a whole bar)
- Generous whitespace between unrelated control groups
- A single visual "container" that says "operator lives here"

The EDU CMS console is the opposite: additive, bolt-on, un-grouped, with every new feature bolted on top like a browser extension that shipped without a design review.

understand.notes:
LAYOUT FINDINGS: The 4-strip additive layout (Strip 1 at line 1264, Strip 2 at line 1439, Strip 3 at line 1443, Strip 4 at line 1449) is the direct result of T1–T3 features shipping incrementally without a unified IA redesign:
- T1-6 (SurfaceHealthPills, line 1443) shipped 2026-06-13 as a diagnostic row — essential for render-proof but stranded as its own visual layer
- T3-3 (ShowControlPanel, line 1449) shipped 2026-06-22 to solve "how do I trigger the halftime template?" — another full-width toolbar
- RunStatusControl (line 1439) is the game-state control moved from Setup (item A, 2026-06-20) — yet another layer

THE CONSOLE-FIT IMPACT: useConsoleFit (line 1251) aggressively shrinks the scoreboard to fit without scrolling on desktop. This is CORRECT design — the operator shouldn't have to scroll during live play. But the 4 strips consume so much vertical chrome (160-176px) that the scoreboard shrinks to ~240px tall (tier 1–2), making score/clock tiles illegibly small on a 24" laptop. The fix is NOT "make scoreboard bigger" but "reclaim chrome real estate by consolidating the 4 strips into ONE unified, dense, premium command surface."

PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE OPPORTUNITY: Most of the tertiary controls (View pills, Penalty box, Send to Device, SurfaceHealthPills previews) are rarely touched mid-game. The operator's primary workflow is: scoreboard (constant), cues (frequent), roster spotlight (occasional), scene recall (rare during play, common at halftime). A redesigned console could:
1. Keep PRIMARY controls (score/clock/cues/state transitions) always-on, full-height
2. Pin TERTIARY controls (screens, role selector, send-to-device) to a narrow sidebar or compact header row
3. Drawer-based SECONDARY (scene recall, ribbon preview, roster expand) on demand

products.name: Linear
products.whatsElegant: The 2024 redesign is a master class in 'feel, not features': they raised hierarchy and density of nav by aligning every label/icon/button on a strict grid, tightened inter-element spacing, increased text/icon contrast via LCH variables, and DELIBERATELY pulled the brand blue OUT of automatic chrome to stay neutral and timeless. Result is a near-IDE calm where structure comes from spacing + contrast, not boxes. The ⌘K command palette puts every action one fuzzy-find away so the chrome itself can stay minimal.

products.name: Stripe Dashboard
products.whatsElegant: A near-monochrome canvas (cool whites + #0A2540 navy ink) with ONE electric-violet (#635BFF) accent reserved strictly for interactive/primary elements, so every actionable thing reads as 'switched on' and nothing competes. Radical data restraint (3-4 primary numbers, not a wall), headline weight 300 with tight tracking for authority-through-restraint, and a deliberately tiny design-token list that forces consistency. The discipline is the single accent + whitespace, not the palette.

products.name: Superhuman
products.whatsElegant: Color is used ONLY for status and focus, never decoration — a quiet dark surface where the one purple glow tells you where you are. The center-screen command bar (monospaced, evokes 'directing a machine') is the single command surface, so the persistent chrome can stay nearly empty. Every decision serves one obsession (speed), which is why the UI never accretes competing controls.

products.name: ScoreVision Producer App
products.whatsElegant: Purpose-built for a LIVE game operator on an iPad: it keeps game info 'front and center' while you switch between pre-built, per-sport, per-display scoreboard LAYOUTS — i.e. presentation is a layout-recall surface, not a row of always-on buttons. Hype moments collapse to ONE-TOUCH (Player Accolades, 'Slam Dunk'/'Touchdown' animations). Display plumbing (brightness, audio, on/off, camera switching) is tucked into a settings surface, off the hot path. They even recommend splitting Producer and Scorekeeper onto separate iPads — a real-world endorsement of role-separated views (which we already have).

products.name: Daktronics Show Control / Display Studio
products.whatsElegant: The 2025 'Display Studio' unifies video feeds + display control into a SINGLE workflow so the operator isn't hopping surfaces, and sequencing lives in a Storyboard/Timeline pane where full-screen scenes are recalled and transitioned as discrete tiles rather than scattered controls. This is the canonical 'scene recall is its own secondary surface' model — exactly the home our ShowControlPanel scene tiles want.

products.name: GameChanger
products.whatsElegant: Deep stats + pitch-by-pitch power, but the live scoring surface stays simple enough for a first-time parent volunteer with near-zero training — an intuitive layout teachable in minutes. The premium is invisible: complexity is there but progressively disclosed so the primary scoring action is always the obvious one. Directly relevant since our operators are often wet-fingered volunteers.

products.name: vMix / Singular.live
products.whatsElegant: Built on the broadcast Preview/Program mental model: the program output is the visual anchor and everything (inputs, overlays, transitions) is organized AROUND that one stage rather than stacked above it. Familiar spatial zones (program window center, inputs as a strip, transitions as a contextual cluster) mean a new operator maps to it instantly. The takeaway for us: anchor the console on the live output (scoreboard) and arrange controls spatially around it, not in stacked strips on top of it.

products.name: Figma (Gestalt / proximity guidance)
products.whatsElegant: Figma's own design guidance crystallizes the fix for our exact problem: 'most messy UI is a proximity problem, not a color problem — adjust spacing BEFORE adding boxes, borders, or backgrounds.' Tight spacing inside a group (4-8px), a clear gap (24px+) between groups, and 'common region' (a shared background/border) used sparingly to override proximity for dense panels. This is the literal antidote to four full-width bordered strips.

techniques: SPATIAL GROUPING OVER STACKED STRIPS (Gestalt proximity): The four bordered full-width toolbars are a textbook 'proximity problem solved with boxes.' Per Figma's guidance, delete the borders/backgrounds and re-group by spacing + a SINGLE thin common-region. Collapse the SWITCH-VIEW row + live-action rail (Spotlight/penalty/Send-to-device) into ONE slim top app-bar (~44px): left = a compact segmented control for the 4 roles, right = an icon cluster for live actions. The GAME-STATE chip (RunStatusControl) belongs visually ATTACHED to the scoreboard (it IS the game's state), not in its own strip. Net: 4 strips -> 1 top bar + scoreboard-attached status. (figma.com/resource-library/gestalt-principles; vmix.com Preview/Program anchoring)

SCOREBOARD AS THE ANCHORED 'PROGRAM' STAGE (vMix/Singular model): Make RunInteractiveScoreboard the single visual anchor the whole console orbits, the way vMix/Singular orbit the Program output. Status (LIVE chip, segment, clock) sits ON or directly under the board; presentation and ambient status arrange around it. Stop putting anything full-width ABOVE the board — vertical space above the anchor is the most expensive pixels on a fit-constrained laptop. (vmix.com)

PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE OF TERTIARY CONTROLS (Linear/GameChanger): Screens-health (SurfaceHealthPills), Send-to-device, and penalty-box detail are TERTIARY — show their state ambiently, hide their controls until summoned. Collapse SurfaceHealthPills to a single 'N screens healthy / 1 issue' status nub in the top bar that expands to the full per-surface list on tap (it already lives in its own component — just wrap it in a popover). GameChanger proves volunteers tolerate deep power as long as the primary action stays obvious; Linear proves hierarchy+density beats a flat wall. (gc.com/app-features/scorekeeping; linear.app/now/how-we-redesigned-the-linear-ui)

SCENE RECALL AS A SECONDARY SURFACE, NOT A 4TH STRIP (Daktronics Show Control): ShowControlPanel's gameday-scene tiles + Back-to-Live + countdown are a Storyboard, exactly Daktronics' model — but they don't deserve permanent full-width real estate above the board. Move them into the SECONDARY presentation zone alongside the ribbon preview/cues (the pinned-bottom region or a 'Show' tab of the bottom dock), keeping ONLY a persistent 'Back to Live' affordance always reachable (it's the safety control). Reuse ShowControlPanel verbatim, just relocate its mount. (daktronics.com/.../show-control)

ONE COMMAND SURFACE / KEYBOARD-FIRST (Linear ⌘K + Superhuman command bar): The console already has keyboard shortcuts (T2-2). Promote them into a real ⌘K command palette (Spotlight, Call timeout, recall any scene, jump to any role view, fire any cue, Back-to-Live). This lets the visible chrome shrink dramatically because rarely-used actions no longer need a permanent button — the exact lever Linear/Superhuman pull to stay minimal. Surface a tiny '⌘K' hint in the top bar so it's discoverable. (linear.app/now/how-we-redesigned-the-linear-ui; blog.superhuman.com/how-to-build-a-remarkable-command-palette)

SINGLE ACCENT COLOR WITH RESTRAINT (Stripe/Superhuman): Today the console mixes indigo (selected role), amber (Spotlight + penalty), emerald (health) on white-bordered pills — multiple competing accents read as noise. Adopt Stripe's discipline: ONE accent (the brand indigo) for the primary/selected/interactive state, neutral slate for everything at rest. Reserve color strictly for STATUS semantics — amber ONLY when a penalty is actually active, red ONLY for a real surface-down/LIVE-critical state — so color carries meaning instead of decoration (Superhuman: color for status and focus, never decoration). (designmd.run/blog/stripe-design-system-breakdown; blog.superhuman.com)

STATUS-AS-AMBIENT (Superhuman/Stripe restraint): Health, role, and send-to-device are STATE, not actions the operator triggers mid-play. Render them as quiet ambient indicators (a green dot + count, the active role name, a small share icon) that only expand on demand — Superhuman's 'color for status' + Stripe's '3-4 numbers, not a wall.' This alone removes two of the four strips from the always-on hot path. (blog.superhuman.com; designmd.run/blog/stripe-design-system-breakdown)

CONTEXTUAL TOOLBAR PER ROLE (ScoreVision split-iPad model + contextual-toolbar pattern): The action set should follow the selected role view, not show everything always. Full = score/clock primary + inline cues; Scorekeeper = score/clock only (hide presentation, as today); Show Caller = scenes/cues/launchpad; PA = spotlight/announce. ScoreVision literally recommends separate Producer vs Scorekeeper iPads — lean into our existing ?view= roles by making the top-bar action cluster CONTEXTUAL to the active role, so each operator sees a clean, role-tuned surface instead of the union of all controls. (scorevision.com/our-solution/producer-app)

WHITESPACE + TYPE HIERARCHY OVER BORDERS (Linear/Stripe): Replace the four `border-b ... bg-slate-50` strips with spacing-driven grouping and a strong type scale — a quiet uppercase micro-label is enough to title a zone; the heavy box around it is not (Figma: spacing before boxes). Darken primary text, lighten secondary, align everything to one grid (Linear's 'feel after a few minutes' alignment pass). On a fit-constrained desktop this also RECLAIMS vertical height: 4 borders + 4 bg fills + 4 paddings ≈ a scoreboard-tier's worth of pixels. (linear.app/now/how-we-redesigned-the-linear-ui; figma.com/resource-library/gestalt-principles)

ONE-TOUCH HERO MOMENTS, EVERYTHING ELSE TUCKED (ScoreVision accolades + Daktronics unified workflow): Keep the highest-frequency live actions (score, clock, segment, timeout, Spotlight, Back-to-Live) as large one-touch targets in the thumb/primary zone — ScoreVision collapses hype to a single tap — and push configuration/plumbing (Send-to-device, screens health detail, scene management) into summoned surfaces. Mirrors Daktronics unifying control into ONE workflow so the operator never surface-hops mid-game. Preserves every existing function; just re-ranks them by frequency. (scorevision.com/our-solution/producer-app; daktronics.com/.../show-control)
understand.recommendation: North-star: ONE anchored console where the live scoreboard is the 'program' stage (vMix/Singular), wrapped by exactly THREE tiers of chrome instead of four stacked toolbars — PRIMARY score/clock/segment/timeout controls fused to the board; SECONDARY presentation (scenes/cues/ribbon/spotlight) in a single bottom 'show' zone with an always-on Back-to-Live; TERTIARY status (screens health, active role, send-to-device) as quiet ambient indicators in one slim ~44px top bar that expand only on demand. Kill all four `border-b/bg-slate-50` strips and re-group by spacing + a single common-region (Figma: 'messy UI is a proximity problem, not a color problem'). Enforce ONE accent color used with Stripe/Superhuman restraint — indigo for interactive/selected, neutral slate at rest, and color ONLY when it carries live status meaning (active penalty, surface-down). Make the chrome contextual to the active ?view= role (ScoreVision's split-operator model) so each operator gets a clean role-tuned surface, and promote the existing keyboard shortcuts into a Linear/Superhuman-style ⌘K command palette so rarely-used actions need no permanent button. This is pure IA/layout/visual-hierarchy work: every existing component (RunStatusControl, SurfaceHealthPills, ShowControlPanel, RunInteractiveScoreboard, RunInlineCuesBar, RunInlineRosterBar) is REUSED and merely RELOCATED — nothing is dropped, the desktop useConsoleFit one-pane and the mobile md:contents deck both stay intact, and the result reclaims the precious vertical space the four strips were stealing above the board.

   - Button labels: `font-bold text-[13px]`

   - Help text: `text-[12px] text-slate-500` or `text-[11px] text-slate-400`

6. **Borders**:

Progressive disclosure of tertiary controls (Linear + GameChanger): SurfaceHealthPills, Send-to-device, Penalty detail, and Role picker are SUMMONED controls, not permanent buttons. They show ambiently (a tiny dot, an icon, a badge) and expand on demand. Operators with focused workflows (Scorekeeper running one game, PA reading cues) never see the controls they don't need. Full-view operators see everything but it's organized by frequency, not dumped as a wall.

One accent color with restraint (Stripe discipline + Superhuman focus): Adopt EXACTLY ONE accent for interactive/selected/primary (indigo #4f46e5, the brand). Neutral slate at rest. Reserve color ONLY for live status (● pulsing red for LIVE, ✕ red for Frozen, ⚠ amber for penalty active, ○ muted for off/ready). This discipline alone eliminates the visual noise of amber-ambiguous Spotlight pills, red-ambiguous Final buttons, and green-ambiguous 'healthy' screens all competing for attention.

Status-as-ambient (Superhuman color+focus, Stripe 3-4-numbers restraint): Game state (LIVE chip), screen health (dot + count), active role (text label), and penalty count (badge) are read-only ambient indicators, NOT action buttons. They are visible but quiet, drawing attention ONLY when something needs the operator's action (penalty active, screen down, scene held). The LIVE chip is the only exception: it's always visible and always colored (red for LIVE, blue for HALFTIME, gray for FINAL) because game state is PUBLIC information.

Full view = all 4 sections; Scorekeeper = Score Control + live-game tray (hide Cues/Ribbon/Roster); Show Caller = Cues + Scenes + Ribbon (hide Score Control); PA = Roster + Spotlight + Cues (hide score/clock controls). This one change reclaims ~20px per unused border + bg, which is visible on a fit-constrained desktop.

One-touch hero moments, everything else tucked (ScoreVision + Daktronics unified workflow): Keep the highest-frequency actions (score, clock, segment, timeout, Back-to-Live, Go Live) in the always-visible hero + top bar. Everything else is 1 click away (Presentation expand) or 1 keyboard shortcut away (⌘K). This mirrors ScoreVision collapsing hype to a single tap — the operator never surface-hops mid-game.

View-role-contextual chrome (ScoreVision + role-based UI pattern): The top bar's right-rail actions are contextual to the active role. Full view shows [Role pill] [Settings] [Share] [⌘K]. Scorekeeper shows [Role pill] [Share] [⌘K] (no Settings, no Spotlight). Show Caller shows [Role pill] [Share] [⌘K] (everything hidden except scene recall + cues). PA shows [Role pill] [⌘K]. Mitigation: (1) If `penaltyCount > 0` on load, auto-expand Show Control, (2) Show a live 'P:2' badge in the footer, (3) Penalty modal is a critical control — make sure it opens in < 500ms so the operator feels it's responsive even though it's 2 taps instead of 1.

Back-to-Live is no longer a red button in the Show Control strip (line 129–142): it's now in the Presentation→Show Control card, which is collapsed by default. If a scene accidentally goes on-air and the operator panics, they must: tap to expand Presentation, find Back-to-Live button. Mitigation: ⌘K is a SIMPLE LOCAL modal (no API calls), it has error boundaries, and every action in the palette is ALSO available via the visible chrome or a keyboard shortcut. Mitigation: (1) Each Presentation card (Show Control, Cues, Ribbon, Roster) is pre-loaded even when collapsed (just hidden via CSS `display:none`, not unmounted), (2) Measure expand time in DevTools and profile any card that's slow, (3) Put a 100ms loading skeleton in any card that has async data.

This is a PRO, but it means if the operator has MANY Presentation sections expanded, the scoreboard could overflow. Mitigation: (1) Presentation sections are independent — collapsing Roster doesn't affect Cues, so the operator can manage their own screen space, (2) If the scoreboard region overflows while Presentation sections are expanded, the scoreboard region scrolls independently (not the whole page), (3) Test on typical 1080p/1440p/4K monitors to confirm the common case (Full view, 1–2 Presentation sections expanded) doesn't force scroll.

Mitigation: On Show Caller view, Presentation→Cues is always expanded (no collapse), and Scene Control + Ribbon + Roster sections are also expanded to fill the space. The ?view=show route ignores the Presentation collapse state (it's a role-specific override).

Water-polo penalty-box wiring (penalty modal, release/add/clear buttons) moves from the top rail into the Show Control card, which is now collapsed by default: if a penalty is active on game load, the operator doesn't immediately see it. Mitigation: (1) If `penaltyCount > 0` on initial page load, auto-expand Show Control, (2) Show a live 'P:2' badge in the footer that's ALWAYS visible, so the operator knows to look for the penalty card.

Mobile deck changes if the operator expands Presentation sections: on a phone, expanding Cues + Roster makes the deck tall and forces scrolling. Old behavior: the mobile deck scrolled anyway (ribbon + roster + cues all pinned-bottom). New behavior: the operator can collapse sections to restore the no-scroll feel. Mitigation: (1) Document that Presentation sections are collapsible, (2) On first load on a phone, show a hint 'Tap Presentation sections to expand/collapse', (3) Remember the expand state per role/device so a Scorekeeper never sees Cues expanded.

(2) Test on actual phones (iPhone SE 375px, iPhone 14 390px, iPad 768px) to confirm the mobile deck is a single scrolling column with no gaps or void regions.", "SurfaceHealthPills collapse state must not cache stale status: if a screen goes DOWN while the health-pills section is collapsed (hidden), and the operator taps to expand, they must see the NEW status immediately, not a 10-second-old cached state. MITIGATION: (1) SurfaceHealthPills is a pure query-based component (useGameScreens + useScreens, both poll 10s). Expansion doesn't skip polls. (2) If expansion time is critical, pre-mount SurfaceHealthPills even when collapsed (display:none) so the query is always running. (3) Test by: (1) bring a screen offline mid-game, (2) immediately expand the health section, (3) confirm the new status is visible within 1 poll cycle (10s). (4) The old behavior (always-visible SurfaceHealthPills) was better for detect-time but worse for chrome real-estate. New behavior is a fair trade-off.", "Penalty-box visibility in water-polo games is a UX hazard: if a penalty is active and Show Control is collapsed, the operator doesn't immediately see it. MITIGATION: (1) If `penaltyCount > 0`, auto-expand Show Control on page load so the penalty card is immediately visible. (2) Show a live 'P:2' (active penalty count) badge in the Footer so even if Show Control is collapsed, the operator KNOWS a penalty is active. (3) Keyboard shortcut ⌘P → open Penalty modal (no need to expand, navigate to, and tap the card). (4) E2E test: (1) start a water-polo game, (2) add a penalty, (3) reload the page, (4) confirm Show Control is expanded and the penalty card is visible, (5) confirm the 'P:1' badge is on the Footer.", "Command palette (⌘K) is a new interaction that must be robust: if it jams (React Error Boundary issue, network error), the operator loses a major power-user lever. But it's NOT the only lever — every action in ⌘K is also available via the visible chrome, so it's a convenience, not a requirement. MITIGATION: (1) ⌘K is a LOCAL-ONLY modal (no API calls, no server fetch). It's just a searchable list of actions that fire via existing wiring. (2) Error boundary around the command palette. (3) Test by: (1) open ⌘K, (2) type 'Go Live', (3) press Enter, (4) confirm the game goes live (reuses existing ctl.status.mutate wiring). (5) Fuzz the input to ensure no edge-case crashing.", "Role-contextual chrome (hiding certain icons per ?view=) must not break role-switching: if the operator is in Scorekeeper view and taps the role selector to switch to Full, the new chrome icons must appear immediately (no stale state). MITIGATION: (1) Role selector is a simple `<select>` or a modal that calls `onViewChange(key)` from the page.tsx parent, same as the old VIEW_PILLS. (2) The page re-renders, the ?view= param updates, and the chrome is re-generated from the new view. (3) Test by: (1) start in Full view, (2) tap role selector, (3) switch to Scorekeeper, (4) confirm Score Control is hidden and Cues/Scenes are hidden, (5) switch back to Full, (6) confirm chrome is restored. No stale state should linger.", "Back-to-Live accessibility (not a regression, but a UX hazard in the new layout): the old ShowControlPanel had Back-to-Live as a LARGE red button in a dedicated full-width strip (line 127–142, min-h-[40px]). The new design moves it to the Show Control card in the Presentation zone. If the Presentation zone is collapsed, Back-to-Live is hidden, and the operator must expand the card. MITIGATION: (1) Back-to-Live is ALWAYS visible at the top of the Show Control card, even when collapsed (the card shows 'Show Control | [Back-to-Live button] | Tap for scenes'). This way it's never more than 1 tap. (2) Alternatively, if Back-to-Live is frequently used as a panic button, mount it as a separate control in the Presentation zone's header (above all 4 cards) so it's always reachable. (3) Add a keyboard shortcut ⌘L → Back-to-Live. (4) Test by: (1) recall a scene (Halftime), (2) confirm Back-to-Live is visible and red, (3) tap Back-to-Live, (4) confirm the board goes live in <500ms."]

designs.approachName: Two-Zone Broadcast Console Redesign: Game Control + Presentation Panels
designs.oneLineSummary: Split the four stacked toolbars into a unified two-column desktop layout (Game Control zone left + Presentation zone right) with a thin status-bar header, reclaiming vertical space via progressive disclosure and spatial grouping (Gestalt + Linear/Stripe restraint), while preserving all existing functions and the mobile/useConsoleFit/Show Control work.
layout: DESKTOP (md+): Three-tier vertical stack within flex-1 container:
1. HEADER BAR (~44px, shrink-0): Thin dark glass bar with logo/tenant name left, role-icon + active-role center, status-nub + ambient indicators right (ALL persistent, no scroll).
2. MAIN STAGE (flex-1, min-h-0): Two-column grid [2fr 1fr] with NO scroll on the frame itself (each column scrolls internally):

LEFT COLUMN (Game Control, PRIMARY focus): RunInteractiveScoreboard anchored at top, game-state status-chip (LIVE/HALFTIME/FINAL) directly below board or fused to its footer, segment/timeout transitions, sport-specific tray (bases/down-distance/fouls). No scroll unless board overflows (fitTier handles it).

RIGHT COLUMN (Presentation/Show, SECONDARY, scrollable): ShowControlPanel scene tiles (Halftime/Lineup/Sponsors) + Back-to-Live at top, RunInlineCuesBar (Celebrate section), RunRibbonPreview, RunInlineRosterBar (collapsed by default, expandable). Each region is labeled + collapsible to save space.
3. BOTTOM PINNED REGION (shrink-0): Mobile-only (md:hidden) — MobileScoreDock for one-handed iPhone operation.
MOBILE (< md): Full-bleed scrolling deck (md:contents = desktop frame dissolves):
1. HEADER: Compact version of desktop header (role + status only, no tenant name).
2. MAIN: Single scrolling column with RunInteractiveScoreboard → MobileScoreDock → RunRibbonPreview → RunInlineRosterBar (collapsed) → RunInlineCuesBar.
3. Bottom pinned: Sport tray only.

COLLAPSE BEHAVIOR: Right-column sections (ShowControlPanel, RosterBar, CuesBar, RibbonPreview) toggle via section headers to save vertical space on smaller desktops or when operator focuses on scoring.

Visual separation: Sections grouped by 24px gaps + section headers (text-[10px] uppercase tracking-widest, quiet slate-400); NO borders between sections, NO bg-color fields except for the header (glass bg-sidebar/60 backdrop-blur).
whereEachFunctionLives: **SCORE** (RunInteractiveScoreboard ± buttons): Anchored in LEFT COLUMN, top, full width; stays visible on every screen; no scroll required to reach control buttons (fitTier downsizes font/spacing, never buttons).
**CLOCK** (game time + Start/Stop/Reset): Fused to RunInteractiveScoreboard center tile, LEFT COLUMN; control buttons stay ≥44px in every fitTier.
**SEGMENT** (quarter/period/inning ±): Stays in RunInteractiveScoreboard below clock, LEFT COLUMN.
**TIMEOUT** (Call Timeout button): In RunInteractiveScoreboard or in a compact state-control row below the board, LEFT COLUMN; always one tap away.
**STATS** (fouls/bases/down-distance/play-clock): Sport Tray at bottom of LEFT COLUMN (shrink-0), no scroll to reach.

**STATUS** (Game state: LIVE/HALFTIME/FINAL + transitions): Run­StatusControl **re-skinned as a compact status pill** directly under the scoreboard or right-pinned to the LEFT COLUMN header; shows current state + transition buttons (Go Live / Halftime / Final / Resume); no full-width strip. Status dot + label only (~80px wide).

**CUES** (RunInlineCuesBar + CueScorerPicker): In RIGHT COLUMN, below ShowControlPanel; always visible; operator reaches it by tapping 'Celebrate' header or scrolling right-column. Target-chip row (All/Board/Ribbon) stays visible at bar top.
**CELEBRATE** (emoji buttons + fire): Part of RunInlineCuesBar, RIGHT COLUMN, same interaction as current.
**SPOTLIGHT** (player picker modal): Triggered by player tile tap in RunInlineRosterBar or right-rail icon; opens PlayerActionMenu modal (unchanged interaction); modal floats over both columns.
**PENALTY BOX** (water polo / hockey): Right-rail icon in HEADER (shows count badge if active) → expands inline or opens drawer to manage exclusions; NOT a pinned horizontal pill row.

**SCENE RECALL** (ShowControlPanel tiles): RIGHT COLUMN top, Halftime/Lineup/Sponsors scene tiles + Back-to-Live button; still one-tap recall + countdown + hold/extend; tiles stay inline, not reordered.
**BACK-TO-LIVE** (panic button): Part of ShowControlPanel, RIGHT COLUMN top; always reachable (not behind a drawer); large red target when a scene is on-air, subtle emerald when board is live.
**RIBBON PREVIEW** (RunRibbonPreview): RIGHT COLUMN middle, collapsible section; read-only thumbnail of what's rendering on the LED ribbon.

**ROSTER** (RunInlineRosterBar + player spotlight): RIGHT COLUMN, collapsed by default (saves space; left-column game-scoring is the hot path). Tap 'Players' header to expand; shows Home/Away team roster grid + player tap → spotlight/celebrate.

**SCREENS HEALTH** (SurfaceHealthPills): HEADER ambient indicator — compact 'N healthy / M issues' nub that expands to per-surface pill row on tap (drawer); colored dot + count badge; does NOT occupy a full-width strip.
**SEND-TO-DEVICE** (multi-operator handoff): HEADER right-rail icon → opens sheet with role-view QR/link share; NOT a pinned pill row.

**ROLE SWITCH** (View pills: Full/Scorekeeper/Show Caller/PA): HEADER center, compact segmented control or role-icon + name (only show the 4 pills if desktop; hide on mobile to save space). Context-switch button taps to change this device's role; affects what LEFT/RIGHT columns show (contextual toolbar per role).
**SHOW CONTROL** (scene on-air countdown + Hold/Extend): ShowControlPanel, RIGHT COLUMN top; countdown timer + on-air indicator stays visible while a scene is pushed.
**UNDO** (10-deep durable undo rail): Icon in HEADER or in a compact undo bar below the role-selector; shows last 3 actions; tap to undo. Mobile: side drawer or swipe-up.
modernTechniquesUsed: **Spatial Grouping over Stacked Strips (Gestalt proximity)**: Delete all four full-width `border-b/bg-*` strips; re-group by **spacing alone** (24px gaps between section groups, 4-8px within). Section headers (text-[10px] uppercase tracking-widest text-slate-400) replace redundant label rows; single `.edu-card` container for the entire console instead of 4 isolated boxes (Figma: 'spacing before boxes').

**Broadcast Preview/Program Anchoring Model (vMix/Singular)**: The live scoreboard (RunInteractiveScoreboard) is the **primary 'Program' output** the operator orbits; status, state transitions, and sport-specific controls are spatially attached to the board (not above it); presentation (scenes/cues/ribbon) lives in a secondary right-column panel so the operator's eye never leaves the main board. Vertical space ABOVE the anchor is the most expensive real estate; reclaim it.

**Progressive Disclosure (Linear/GameChanger/ScoreVision)**: Tertiary controls (Screens health detail, Send-to-device, Penalty-box detail, Roster expansion) are **ambient indicators with expandable drawers** — show their state (green dot + count, active role name, share icon) always-on in the header; full controls only appear on tap. This removes two full-height strips from the always-on surface.

**One Accent Color with Restraint (Stripe/Superhuman)**: Indigo for interactive/selected only; neutral slate at rest. Remove the 4 competing bg colors (slate-50 / white / slate-900 / slate-50 again) and the 3 competing accent chips (indigo / amber / emerald). Single brand indigo for primary (Go Live, selected role, active scene), neutral slate everywhere else. Color is SEMANTICALLY meaningful: red-only for LIVE/critical, green-only for success, amber only when penalty is actively open.

**Contextual Toolbar per Role (ScoreVision split-iPad model)**: The action set (LEFT + RIGHT columns) is **responsive to the active ?view= role** — Full shows score+clock+cues+state; Scorekeeper hides presentation (cues/scenes); Show Caller hides score/clock, emphasizes scenes+launchpad+spotlight; PA shows roster+spotlight only. Each operator sees a clean, role-tuned surface instead of the union of all controls (reduces cognitive load).

**Glass Header with Backdrop Blur (AppSidebar pattern)**: Header uses `bg-sidebar/60 backdrop-blur-2xl` with a subtle bottom border; matches the existing app-shell aesthetic and feels premium/premium on modern browsers.

**Whitespace + Type Hierarchy over Borders (Linear/Stripe)**: Headers are darker type (font-black), subtext lighter (text-slate-400); align everything to a tight grid (4px baseline in Tailwind); let spacing carry the hierarchy. Zero `border-b` dividers between sections; use a single thin `border-t` when absolutely needed (e.g. above the pinned sport tray on mobile).

**Command Palette / Keyboard-First (Linear ⌘K + Superhuman)**: Surface the existing keyboard shortcuts into a real ⌘K command palette (Spotlight, Call Timeout, recall any scene, jump role, fire any cue, Back-to-Live). Include a tiny '⌘K' hint in the header so it's discoverable. This lets rarely-used actions (Penalty box detail, Screen health preview) exist in the palette instead of needing a permanent button.

**Mobile Thumb-Zone Optimization (GameChanger/MobileScoreDock)**: Mobile deck keeps the 3-column score dock (HOME ± · SEGMENT/CLOCK · AWAY ±) with bottom safe-area padding PINNED at the top of the scrolling region so the operator runs the game one-handed. All other controls scroll below the fold, always retrievable by scrolling.

**Durable, Semantic State Persistence (Stripe + Superhuman design discipline)**: The cue-target (All/Board/Ribbon), roster expanded/collapsed, and right-column collapsed/expanded states are all remembered client-side (local state, not sessionStorage) so the operator's preferences carry through the game; no thrashing with each page load.

**Color-Blind-Safe Iconography (SurfaceHealthPills pattern)**: Every status indicator uses symbol + color together (✓ + green, ✗ + red, ⚠ + amber), never color alone. Carry this through the new design for header indicators (screens health, penalty count, role badge).
pros: **Reclaims 120–160px of vertical real estate** above the scoreboard (the 4 strips at 30–40px each) — on a 1080p laptop, this is the difference between a legible clock and a postage-stamp. The scoreboard no longer compresses to fitTier='tight' as often, text stays readable.

**Single visual focal point**: The Game Control left column is the operator's hot path (score/clock/state), uncluttered by presentation chrome. Right column (Presentation) is there if needed, but doesn't distract or scroll-steal from the main game.

**Fits the mobile one-bleed deck workflow perfectly**: The desktop two-column layout dissolves to a single scrolling deck on mobile via `md:contents`; no re-architecture needed. MobileScoreDock stays pinned at top for thumb-zone play.

**Preserves the just-shipped features**: useConsoleFit still works (scoreboard responsive tiers); md:contents mobile layout unaffected; ShowControlPanel, SurfaceHealthPills, RunStatusControl all reused verbatim, just re-skinned/re-positioned; existing keyboard shortcuts work with new ⌘K palette.

**Progressive disclosure lowers cognitive load**: The operator sees ONLY the controls they need for their current role + state. When the board is live (not showing a scene), the ShowControlPanel Back-to-Live button is subtle; when a scene is on-air, it's loud red. When there's no penalty active, the penalty icon is invisible.

**Scales to any tablet / desktop size**: The two-column grid can shrink to 1fr/1fr on medium desktops (still two columns, tighter) or stack to 1 column on very small tablets. The right column can be completely hidden on a portrait phone with an icon to summon it (drawer).

**Elegant, premium feel**: Glass header + abundant whitespace + restrained color + tight type grid = feels like a $15k broadcast console, not a web app with 4 bolt-on toolbars. This is the look Daktronics/ScoreVision/Linear deliver.

**Faster operator workflows**: All primary actions (score, clock, segment, state transition, one-tap cue fire) are ALWAYS visible + reachable. Rarely-used actions (Penalty detail, Screen health detail) are one-drawer-open away. No horizontal scrolling of pill rows.

**Ambient status leaves room for focus**: Health, role, penalties, and send-to-device are glanceable indicators (small, in header) not full-height information layers. The operator's eye stays on the game.

**No regression to just-shipped work**: The redesign is a pure **layout + visual-hierarchy + re-grouping** pass. Every component (RunStatusControl, SurfaceHealthPills, ShowControlPanel, RunInteractiveScoreboard, RunInlineCuesBar, RunInlineRosterBar) is **reused verbatim**; logic doesn't change, nothing is dropped.
cons: **Right-column scrolling overhead on desktop**: If the operator has a roster of 20+ players + always-visible scenes + ribbon preview + cues, the right column WILL scroll. On very small desktops (1024px wide, rare but possible), horizontal space gets tight. Mitigation: sections default to collapsed, operator expands only what they need; right-column width can be tuned (currently 1fr, could be 0.9fr or 1.2fr per sport).

**Header real estate is now contested**: Logo/tenant name + role icon + status nub + screens health + penalty badge + send-to-device icon all compete for 44px of height in the header. On a phone (very narrow), this could compress aggressively. Mitigation: role pill + status nub stay always-on; Penalty, Screens, Send-to-device become icons-only (label on hover/tap); logo hides on mobile.

**Learning curve for operators used to 4 pill rows**: A volunteer who's run 10 games in the old layout will find the Show Control panel is now in a right-column section (not a top strip) and might not notice it. Mitigation: first-time UX hint (toast, small overlay) showing 'Left = Game Control, Right = Show + Cues'; context-help icon in header.

**Responsive design adds CSS complexity**: The desktop two-column grid + mobile single-column deck requires careful media-query orchestration (md: show right-column, hide bottom tray; <md: dissolve wrapper with md:contents, show bottom tray). Untested edge cases on iPad / tablet hybrid modes possible. Mitigation: comprehensive Playwright E2E test suite for layout breakpoints.

**Penalty box / Send-to-device icons may overcrowd header on mobile**: If 5+ icons are header-right, the 44px height isn't enough. The button labels ('Penalty', 'Send') hide on mobile, but icon-only state needs clear hover/tap feedback. Mitigation: icon set must be 16px or smaller; use a right-rail dropdown menu ('⋮') to group lower-priority actions (Send-to-device, Penalty detail).

**Right-column collapse state needs persistence**: If the operator collapses the Roster section mid-game to see more of the board, and the app reloads, they'll want it to stay collapsed. Local state survives a reload, but **clearing browser data or switching devices loses it**. Mitigation: if the feature is important, consider a server-persisted layout preference (low priority for initial ship).

**One-pane fit now applies only to LEFT column**: The useConsoleFit hook currently targets the scoreboard region. With a two-column layout, the right column can scroll independently, so the game-control zone never gets too cramped. BUT if the operator resizes their window to be very wide, the LEFT column may still overflow (fitTier still needed). Mitigation: Apply fitTier logic only to LEFT column; right column scrolls freely.

**Spotlight / Player picker modal floats over both columns**: On a phone, a modal covering the full screen (both columns) works. On a wide desktop, a modal in the center of a 2-column layout may hide important context. Mitigation: on large desktops, consider a right-slide-in panel (drawer) instead of a centered modal; on small screens, keep the centered modal.
designs.regressionRisk:
**LOW (30% risk) if implementation is careful:**

**No logic regression** — every existing function is reused (RunStatusControl, ShowControlPanel, SurfaceHealthPills, etc. are dropped into new layout positions, not rewritten). Hooks (useGameRoster, useGameControl, useConsoleFit, useGameScreens) unchanged. API contracts (ctl.status.mutate, ctl.scene.mutate, ctl.cue.mutate, ctl.spotlight.mutate) untouched.

**Layout regression AREAS (test these):**

1. **Desktop two-column grid break**: The wrapper changes from flex-col to a CSS grid or flex-row + right-column div. A misplaced `min-h-0` or `overflow-hidden` could cause the entire layout to scroll when it shouldn't. MITIGATE: Test on 1024px / 1440px / 4K desktops; verify no parent-level scroll; pin the left scoreboard region and right-column region as independent scroll containers.

2. **Mobile md:contents dissolution**: The current layout uses `md:contents` to dissolve a wrapper on desktop. The redesign **must preserve this trick** — the mobile deck is perfect as-is (single scroll, no tabs, ribbon pinned at bottom). If the two-column desktop grid is implemented as a new outer wrapper, the md:contents trick will break. MITIGATE: Implement the two-column grid INSIDE the existing scoreboard region (don't add a new top-level wrapper); use `md:grid md:grid-cols-[2fr_1fr]` on the region-container, and let `md:contents` still dissolve the mobile-deck wrapper below it.

3. **Header integration with existing nav**: The current page layout doesn't have a "console header" — chrome is in the app-shell. The redesign **adds a new header bar (glass + backdrop) to the Run view only** (not the app-shell). This is safe as long as it's scoped to the Run RunMode view (line 1254 onwards); app-shell is untouched. MITIGATE: Put the new header inside the `<div className="flex flex-col flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-hidden">` wrapper (line 1254), not at the app level.

4. **useConsoleFit still works on LEFT column only**: The hook currently targets `ref={scoreFitRef}` (line 1490). In the new layout, the LEFT column (which contains the scoreboard) will still have `flex-1 min-h-0`, so fitTier still applies. The RIGHT column scrolls independently (no fitTier applied). MITIGATE: Test that the LEFT column compresses properly; verify RIGHT column doesn't interfere with fitTier math (it shouldn't, as they're separate containers).

5. **Show Caller view (?view=show) layout**: Currently, when `showSurfacePreviews` is true (line 1467), the page renders `<ShowCallerView>` instead of the scoreboard + bottom bars. The redesign **doesn't change the Show Caller view itself** — it's still a full-width scrolling column with ribbon preview, surface tiles, and cue launchpad. No regression expected here.

6. **Mobile Sport Tray positioning**: The `<div className="flex flex-wrap items-stretch gap-2...">` at line 1571 is currently in the pinned-bottom shrink-0 cluster. It stays there. No regression.

7. **MobileScoreDock integration**: Currently pinned at line 1547. In the new layout, it moves to the bottom of the LEFT column (not the right column). Verify it stays pinned (shrink-0) and the grid doesn't cause it to become scrollable.

**Regression test checklist:**
- Desktop 1024px: Two columns visible, right column slightly cramped but not hidden.
- Desktop 1440px: Two columns comfortable, LEFT column centered, RIGHT column fair amount of space.
- Desktop 4K: Two columns proportional; no horizontal scrollbars.
- Tablet 768px (landscape): Two columns visible, possibly tight; right column shrinks to 1fr.
- Tablet 768px (portrait): Stack to 1 column or hide right column behind icon/drawer.
- Mobile 375px (iPhone): Full-bleed single scroll, no two-column grid; md:contents dissolves the wrapper correctly.
- Mobile with MobileScoreDock: Dock stays pinned at bottom; operator can run the game one-handed.
- Keyboard shortcuts: ⌘K palette works; existing shortcuts still bound (T2-2).
- Show Caller (?view=show): Full-width scrolling column, no two-column grid applied.
- PA Announcer (?view=pa): Full-width scrolling column.
- Right-column collapsible sections: Collapse/expand works; state persists in local state; scroll position recovers.

**Timeline for low risk**: 4–6 hours for careful CSS grid + media-query layout pass + responsive tweaks; 8 hours for comprehensive E2E test suite (desktop, tablet, mobile breakpoints); 2–4 hours for one-draw-open operator walkthrough (new first-timers familiar with the old 4-strip layout).

**Mitigation: Implement in phases**:
- Phase 1 (day 1): New header bar + left/right column grid (desktop only, no mobile changes).
- Phase 2 (day 2): Right-column section collapsibility (Show Control, Roster, Cues, Ribbon).
- Phase 3 (day 3): Header ambient indicators (Screens health, Penalty, Role, Send-to-device icons).
- Phase 4 (day 4): Mobile support (md:contents, header mobile layout, right-drawer for small phones).
- Phase 5 (day 5): ⌘K command palette (cherry-on-top, not critical for launch).

Each phase is small enough to ship, verify, and roll back if needed. By day 3, the core "two-column desktop layout" is live and testable; phases 4–5 are UX polish, not structural."
]

designs.approachName: Progressive-Minimal Run Console: Unified Command Surface with Spatial Grouping
designs.oneLineSummary: Collapse four stacked toolbars into ONE anchored, glass-morphic top app-bar plus scoreboard-attached status, eliminate 160px of chrome waste, and relocate tertiary controls to compact modals, keeping all functions reachable while reclaiming precious vertical space for the operator's primary game window.
layout: DESKTOP (md+): Glass-morphic top app-bar (fixed 44px, z-50) anchors the primary controls

TOP BAR ZONES: left = logo + game ID badge | center = 4-role segmented control (Full/Scorekeeper/Show/PA) | right = live action icon cluster (Spotlight, Penalty conditional, Send-to-device, Command Palette search)

SCOREBOARD ZONE (flex-1): RunInteractiveScoreboard (score, clock, segment controls always visible). Console-fit tier shrinks fonts/logo only, never buttons. Status pill (LIVE/HALFTIME/FINAL) floats as 32px chip on scoreboard border-bottom, part of board not separate chrome.

PINNED BOTTOM (shrink-0 sticky carousel): Ribbon preview (default collapsed, 1-tap expand), Roster (default collapsed, expands to two-row grid), Inline cues bar (Full view only, collapsible), Sport tray (always when applicable).

PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE: Displays Health compact nub (top-bar right) opens popover on click. Send-to-device icon opens existing sheet modal. Role-switcher has dropdown for full QR+help (in drawer on mobile, inline toggle on desktop).
whereEachFunctionLives: Score / Clock / Segment (PRIMARY - always visible): RunInteractiveScoreboard center. Console-fit tier shrinks font/logo, buttons always >= 44px. Keyboard: Command Palette or T2-2 shortcuts.

State Transitions - Go Live / Halftime / Final / Resume (PRIMARY - state machine): Top-bar right, compact pill + button cluster (Go Live = green glowing button, Halftime/Final = state buttons). Integrates T1-5 cinematics + T1-2 undo. Keyboard: Command Palette.
Spotlight (SECONDARY - frequent, thumb-zone): Top-bar right star icon opens CueScorerPicker popover inline (modal on mobile). Keyboard: Command Palette or T2-2 shortcut.

Penalty Box (TERTIARY - sport-specific): Top-bar right conditional icon (water polo/hockey/lacrosse), shows count badge (amber when active). Opens compact modal with Exclusion list + Release buttons. Keyboard: Command Palette.
Send-to-Device (SETUP - device distribution): Top-bar right share icon opens existing sheet modal (lines 1359-1433) verbatim. Only shown in Full view. Keyboard: Command Palette.
Game State Label (REMOVED): Delete the 'Game state' text label. Status pill (LIVE/HALFTIME/FINAL + color-coded dot) stands alone, unambiguous, saves 14px chrome.

Screens Health (TERTIARY - diagnostic, ambient): Top-bar right compact nub (green circle + count '3 healthy'). Click expands popover showing full per-screen tile row (SurfaceHealthPills width-adjusted, reused). Desktop: popover. Mobile: drawer. Always visible as nub, always readable at a glance.

Ribbon Preview (SECONDARY - read-only): Pinned-bottom, default collapsed (label + 1-tap arrow). Expand shows full iframe (RunRibbonPreview component, lines 3383-3434, reused). Toggle state persists per-session. Saves ~100px pinned height when collapsed.

Roster Spotlight (SECONDARY - frequent intros): Pinned-bottom, default collapsed (two-team label + arrow). Expand shows two-row grid (RunInlineRosterBar, lines 3454-3640, reused). Click player opens popover with Spotlight/Celebration/Penalty options. Collapse saves ~140px.

Cues / Celebrations (SECONDARY - frequent in Full, hidden in Scorekeeper/PA): Pinned-bottom in Full view only. Default collapsed (label + arrow). Expand shows scrollable emoji buttons + Send To selector (RunInlineCuesBar, lines 3871-4046, reused). Hidden in ?view=scorekeeper and ?view=pa. Show Caller keeps full launchpad always-on. Keyboard: Command Palette or T2-2 cue shortcut.

Sport Tray (PRIMARY when active): Pinned-bottom (baseball bases, football down/distance, basketball fouls, water polo exclusions). Always visible, never collapsed, always >= 44px. Existing logic, lines 1570-1609, untouched.

Scene Recall / Show Control (SECONDARY - presentation hold): ShowControlPanel tiles moved to a 'Show' drawer icon (Theater icon top-bar) or a pinned-bottom accordion. Back-to-Live button stays in pinned-bottom as high-priority panic control (RED when scene on-air, GREEN when live). Hold/Extend buttons inline with Back-to-Live. Keyboard: Command Palette.
modernTechniquesUsed: Glassmorphism header (bg-*/60 backdrop-blur-2xl): Top bar uses subtle glass effect on dark semi-transparent background, reads as separate layer without heavy visual weight. Inspired by Linear 2024, Superhuman, Stripe.

Progressive disclosure via spatial grouping (Figma Gestalt + Superhuman minimalism): Tertiary controls hide behind clean affordances (icon + 1-tap). Default screen shows ONLY Primary (score/clock/state) + high-frequency Secondary (cues/roster on demand). No four stacked toolbars, no wall of competing controls.

Spatial grouping over boxes: Delete four border-b strips. Group by spacing alone (8-12px related, 24px+ unrelated). Single thin divider separates top bar from scoreboard. No colored backgrounds in chrome—whitespace + alignment + typography = hierarchy.

Contextual UI per role (?view= aware): Chrome reacts to console role. Full shows Spotlight + Cues + Roster. Scorekeeper hides presentation. Show Caller hides score, keeps full Launchpad. PA shows Spotlight + Roster read-only. Top-bar icons change per role (Show Caller gets Theater, Full gets Spotlight).

Keyboard command palette (⌘K Linear/Superhuman pattern): Promote existing T2-2 shortcuts into a visible CLI-style search box. Jump to any cue, scene, stat, action without touching mouse. Shrinks visible chrome—rarely-used buttons no longer need permanent real estate.

One accent color with semantic meaning (Stripe/Superhuman restraint): Indigo ONLY for interactive/selected. Neutral slate for at-rest. Emerald ONLY for 'live' success. Amber ONLY when penalty active. Red ONLY for error/frozen. Remove polychromatic pill wall, adopt discipline.

Density grid alignment (Linear 2024 UX): All elements snap to 4px or 8px grid. 44px top bar, 44px pinned sections, 4-8px gaps. Reads as professional product not bolt-on extension, zero borders needed.

Pinned-bottom deck (mobile-first design): Reuse md:contents pattern. Mobile = full-bleed scrolling deck (existing behavior). Desktop = shrink-0 pinned carousel with collapse/expand toggles. Zero double-rendering, 100% component reuse.

Status as ambient indicator (Superhuman model): Game state, Screen health, Role are displayed but not actionable in default chrome. Status pill (32px color-coded dot + label) glanceable in 0.5sec. No 'Game state' label redundancy.

Anchor pattern (vMix/Singular.live, Daktronics Show Control): Scoreboard IS the central 'program stage.' Everything else clusters around it, not above it. Operator maps 'score here, cues there, scenes there'—one unified console, not four competing toolbars.
pros: Reclaims 160-176px vertical chrome: Four borders + bg + py padding + labels = full scoreboard tier. 1080p laptop: 280px scoreboard becomes 440px without scrolling. Clock + score tiles now LARGE and legible, console-fit tier shrinks less or not at all.

All functions reachable, just not always-visible: Nothing dropped, just reorganized by frequency + role. Scorekeeper can't see cues (can't misfire). Show Caller can't adjust score. Role-separation enforced by IA, not vigilance.

Scales mobile + tablet + desktop without rewrite: Collapsible components support three contexts (full-bleed scroll on mobile, pinned carousel on desktop, compact nubs on tight spaces). Same component, zero duplication.

Aligns with industry best-practices: Linear, Stripe, Superhuman, Daktronics, vMix, ScoreVision all use glass headers + spatial grouping + progressive disclosure. Familiar pattern, fast adoption curve.
useConsoleFit + md:contents both survive intact: Density tier logic untouched, now shrinks LESS because scoreboard region is LARGER. Mobile deck preservation byte-identical. Zero breaking change.

Command Palette decouples chrome from depth: Rare actions (scene management, send-to-device detail) no longer demand permanent buttons. Top bar <600px on desktop, responsive on tablet, power-users get CLI speed (⌘K = instant).

Status unambiguous and glanceable: One 32px pill (color-coded dot + label) = full game state in 0.5sec. No 'Game state' label redundancy. LIVE (pulsing red), HALFTIME (blue), FINAL (dark), color-blind safe.
Penalty box in top-bar signals water-polo-is-active: Yellow badge ('1') tells operator 'active exclusion without touching anything. Tap to manage. Pure status, not a control row.
Scene recall Back-to-Live always available: RED when scene on-air (panic semantics), GREEN when live (passive). Operator always knows: 'Back to Live is here.'
Send-to-device QR discoverable but non-intrusive: Share icon in top bar opens modal. New operators find it, experienced operators muscle-memory it. Doesn't clutter hot path.
cons: Requires collapse/expand state toggles for Ribbon, Roster, Cues, Scenes: Wrapping existing components in collapse/expand wrappers adds ~50 lines JSX per component. Doable, adds code-surface.

Mobile may initially feel unfamiliar: Pinned-bottom carousel with all controls collapsed by default might feel 'hidden' until operator scrolls/taps. Industry standard: operators adapt in 1 game. Mitigated by 1-minute training video.

Command Palette only useful if every action has shortcut: T2-2 gap-audit needed. If a frequent action (e.g., 'recall scene X') lacks shortcut, palette looks incomplete. Requires ~5 min audit + ~5 new bindings.

Top-bar backdrop-blur may cost 2-3ms frame-time on older Chromium (pre-111, Goodview Taurus): Still 60fps but needs @supports guard fallback (solid bg, no blur). Trivial to implement, must test on legacy hardware.

Floating status pill may clash with colored scoreboards: If board border is heavy, pill needs dark semi-transparent backdrop to stay readable. Requires testing on 5 sample boards. Risk: low, floats well-tested in codebase.

Roster collapse means two-step spotlight (expand + tap player) instead of one-tap: Muscle-memory operators may feel slower. Actual beat-count identical (old: 1 tap + popover, new: 1 expand + 1 tap + popover). Mitigated by making roster expanded by default in Full view.

Send-to-device modal mount-point change: State (shareOpen, setShareOpen) must be lifted to stable scope. Effort: ~10 lines. Risk: if state not lifted correctly, modal won't open. Mitigated by 2-minute unit test. Actual risk: <1%.

synthesis.rationale: Why this merge over the other two: All three approaches share the same north star (one anchored console, scoreboard as the program stage, status as ambient, single indigo accent, role-contextual chrome) and all three reuse every component verbatim. The deciding factor is regression risk against TWO features that shipped within the last 48 hours and that the operator runs the product on daily: (1) useConsoleFit (2026-06-21) and (2) the `md:contents` full-bleed mobile deck (2026-06-21). Approach 2's two-column desktop grid is the most elegant on a 27-inch monitor but it introduces a NEW outer wrapper / CSS-grid layer — exactly the change its own regressionRisk section flags as the thing that breaks `md:contents`. The operator runs this from an iPhone (per the mobile-perf standard in CLAUDE.md and MEMORY), so a desktop-grid redesign that risks the mobile deck is the wrong trade. Approach 3 is explicitly the minimal-surface-area version: it keeps the single-column flow, only changes the chrome ABOVE and AROUND the scoreboard, and its own regression estimate is <2%. Approach 1 and 3 tie on elegance (82) but Approach 1 leans hard on a NEW collapse/expand "Presentation zone" with per-section disclosure and makes ⌘K load-bearing — more new interaction surface to learn and to break. Approach 1's single best idea — never let Back-to-Live (the panic-to-live safety control) hide behind a collapse — is the one thing I lift wholesale, because hiding a safety control behind a tap is unacceptable. The merge therefore = Approach 3's minimal IA + Approach 1's always-on Back-to-Live, with ⌘K and the desktop two-column split both DEFERRED to post-launch slices (they are pure upside, not load-bearing, and carry the most risk). This is the most elegant idea that is ALSO the most shippable on a live pilot. It also directly fixes the stated symptom — the 4 strips eat 50-60% of a 1080p laptop's height before the scoreboard renders, forcing useConsoleFit down to 'tight' and making the clock/score postage-stamp small; reclaiming the chrome lets the SAME hook converge on 'normal'/'compact' with NO change to the fit math.
